holidays.name: Towel Day
holidays.description: Fans of Douglas Adams carry a towel with them all day long to honor the author of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Towels get draped over shoulders, tucked into backpacks, and waved proudly in offices and on public transit.
holidays.origin: Started in 2001, two weeks after Douglas Adams died on May 11, 2001. Fans organized the tribute online, and it has been held every year since.
holidays.funFact: In the books, a towel is described as the most useful item an interstellar hitchhiker can have, since it can be used for warmth, as a weapon, or as a signal for rescue.

holidays.name: Geek Pride Day
holidays.description: A celebration of geek culture, from sci-fi and fantasy fans to gamers, coders, and science enthusiasts. Participants are encouraged to proudly embrace their nerdy passions without apology.
holidays.origin: It first appeared in Spain in 2006 as Orgullo Friki, chosen to coincide with the anniversary of the 1977 release of Star Wars. It later spread to other countries, and the day is now tied to Towel Day as well.
holidays.funFact: The date was picked because it is the anniversary of the original Star Wars premiering on May 25, 1977, and it is also Towel Day, so geeks get a double celebration.

holidays.name: National Wine Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day to uncork a bottle of your favorite red, white, rosé, or sparkling wine. Wine lovers raise a glass, try a new variety, or visit a vineyard.
holidays.origin: It is an informal food and drink observance popularized in the United States through social media and food-holiday calendars, with no single official founder.
holidays.funFact: Wine has been made for thousands of years, and the oldest known winery was found in a cave in Armenia, dating back about 6,100 years.

holidays.name: National Missing Children's Day
holidays.description: A day of awareness to remember missing children and to encourage families, schools, and communities to focus on child safety. Many people wear blue or forget-me-not flowers.
holidays.origin: Established in the United States in 1983 by President Ronald Reagan after the disappearance of Etan Patz in 1979. May 25 was chosen as the anniversary of his disappearance.
holidays.funFact: The date is also observed internationally as International Missing Children's Day, and the forget-me-not flower is used as a symbol of the cause.

holidays.name: National Tap Dance Day
holidays.description: A day to shuffle, ball-change, and clatter your way through the streets in honor of tap dancing. Dance studios hold performances and free classes to celebrate the rhythmic art form.
holidays.origin: Signed into U.S. law in 1989 by President George H. W. Bush. The date honors the birthday of Bill 'Bojangles' Robinson, born May 25, 1878.
holidays.funFact: Bill 'Bojangles' Robinson famously danced up and down a staircase in films with Shirley Temple, and he once ran 100 yards backward in 13 seconds.
